subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity SLOs & perf validation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@acme.com>; ACME Infra Team <infra-eng@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity SLOs & perf validation

Samantha / team —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the Dedicated capacity validation run. High-level from the call:

- Goals: validate Dedicated capacity sizing to meet your latency SLOs for streamed token-by-token responses and quantify reserved throughput (tokens/sec) required to sustain peak concurrency while hitting p95 latency targets.
- Workload details you shared: ~120 QPS peak, model family: open-llama-13B-ish, average prompt+response ~512 tokens, streaming enabled for UX.

Action items & asks from Redwood:
1) Confirm target SLOs for the validation run (see options below).
   - Option A (strict): p50 < 60ms, p95 < 200ms end-to-end per-token latency (streaming), sustain 50 concurrent streams.
   - Option B (balanced): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms, sustain 100 concurrent streams.
2) Provide representative prompt set and example bundle of requests (we can use a subset for warm cache and worst-case for cold cache).
3) Sign-off on the test plan so we can schedule lab time (we usually run on H100 and A100 for comparison).

Proposed Redwood test matrix (tentative):
- GPUs: NVIDIA H100 80GB, A100 40GB, L4 (if you want a cost-focused baseline).
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95 token latency, end-to-end generation latency, tokens/sec throughput, memory utilization, GPU saturation, tail latency under burst traffic, and streaming gap/jitter.
- Test vectors: cold-start runs, warm-cache sustained run (30m), concurrency ramp to peak, and spike tests (2x peak for 2 minutes).

Attached: perf-requirements-template.xlsx (fill in your SLO choices + peak traffic windows).

Next step: can you reply with confirmed SLO targets and attach the sample prompts? If useful, we can also run a quick pre-check with a 1-hour smoke run next Tuesday or Wednesday — we have a 4–6pm PT slot available.

Thanks — looping Aditya to help lead the validation.

—Marissa

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. A few answers inline and attached a sample prompt set.

- SLOs: we want the strict option if possible. Target is p95 < 200ms for per-token latency with streaming enabled. p50 ideally < 60ms.
- Concurrency/Throughput: our UX opens ~50 concurrent users during peak; each stream produces ~10–12 tokens/sec on average. Peak QPS ~120 requests/sec (burst to ~240 for short windows).
- Model: we expect to run a 13B open model variant (not the largest), quantized FP16/8.
- Prompts: attached acme-sample-prompts.txt (mix of short and long prompts; avg ~300 tokens).

We can do the smoke pre-check on Tuesday 2026-10-13 in the morning PST. We should also verify any compliance checklist before granting access to corp data (we'll coordinate with security).

Also: can Redwood propose a recommended reserved throughput (tokens/sec) and how many dedicated GPUs we'd need to commit for 24/7 vs peak-burst sizing? We may want pricing as part of the next step.

—Samantha
Samantha Lopez
Head of Product Integrations, ACME Corp
samantha.lopez@acme.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity SLOs & perf validation

Samantha — perfect, thanks for confirming and for the prompt file. Looping Aditya and Monica to propose the concrete test plan and estimate reserved throughput.

Aditya / Monica — see ACME's confirmed targets above: p95 < 200ms (per-token streaming), p50 < 60ms, sustain ~50 concurrent streams, peak QPS ~120 (brief bursts to 240). Prompts attached.

Suggested Redwood test plan (we can update after your input):
1) GPU comparison: run identical workload on H100 (80GB), A100 (40GB), and L4-class (cost baseline) to measure per-token latency and GPU utilization.
2) Reserved throughput sizing: start with a conservative baseline of 60k tokens/sec reserved throughput for steady-state to cover 50 concurrent streams + overhead; run scale tests to identify the breakpoints where p95 slips beyond 200ms.
3) Concurrency profile: 50 steady concurrent streams (sustained 30m), then 2-minute spikes to 240 QPS, then ramp down.
4) Streaming specifics: we will measure token-to-token latency (stream jitter), and end-to-end time-to-first-token.
5) Validation deliverables: CSV with latency percentiles, GPU metrics, model memory headroom, and recommendation for committed GPU count and type (e.g., 3x H100 for 24/7 if needed).

A couple of questions for ACME before we lock lab time:
- Typical generation length per response (you said ~512 tokens average; the sample looks slightly shorter — can you confirm distribution?).
- Are you using any heavy on-request tools (e.g., external DB calls) that would affect end-to-end latency?

Proposed schedule: pre-check smoke run on Tue 2026-10-13 (AM PT). Full validation window Wed–Thu (we can reserve 4–6 H100 hours for the main run).

Attaching our standard test plan: redwood-lab-test-plan.pdf. Samantha — we'll send an initial sizing estimate once Aditya runs a quick projection based on the sample prompts.

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Samantha — copied the test plan and ran a quick projection from the sample prompts. High-level findings / ask before we book the main lab run: 

Quick projection (ballpark):
- Model: open-llama-13B FP16-like performance. On an H100 80GB instance we expect ~700–900 tokens/sec per GPU under streaming micro-batched runtime for 1–2 concurrent streams per GPU core; actual numbers depend on quantization and kernel selection.
- To meet 60k tokens/sec baseline we estimate needing ~7–9 H100 GPUs (conservative), ~10–12 A100 40GB GPUs, or ~14–18 L4-class inference instances (if available) — these are rough; main validation will refine.
- For sustained 50 concurrent streams your primary concern will be tail latency under burst; we'll instrument without tooling overhead to isolate model runtime latency.

Proposed concrete lab run items:
1) Smoke: 30 minutes on 1x H100 using your prompt sample to validate end-to-end pipeline and streaming behavior.
2) GPU matrix: run 30–60 minute sustained runs at ~50 concurrent streams on H100, A100, and L4; collect p50/p90/p95/p99 token latencies and GPU metrics.
3) Throughput ramp: sweep tokens/sec from 10k to 120k to find saturation point for p95 > 200ms.
4) Burst test: 2-minute 2x peak spike to characterize tail.

Pre-reqs we need from ACME:
- A small set of 100 representative prompts (you already attached — thanks). Please confirm distribution (short/median/long) and whether you expect hallucination-safe decoding params.
- Access window for lab: Tue AM for smoke; Wed/Thu for full runs. Confirm which time zone works.

Next: if ACME confirms Tue morning smoke we will provision and share a lab run calendar invite and the pre-run checklist (no sensitive production data required). After the matrix we will deliver a sizing recommendation (committed GPUs + suggested reserved throughput) and cost estimate.

—Aditya
